title: Candidate Touchpoint & Offer Velocity Playbook — Q2 2026
content:
Purpose:
This playbook outlines an operational baseline for candidate touchpoints and offer velocity across technical and product hiring at Redwood Inference. Goal: reduce time-to-offer, improve candidate experience, and standardize recruiter / hiring-manager responsibilities without sacrificing quality of hire.

Scope:
- Applies to IC and manager-level hires for engineering, product, and applied-ML teams in hosted/dedicated/private product areas.
- Excludes executive / C-suite and external agency-managed searches (separate SOP).

High-level targets (service level agreements):
- A: Initial recruiter outreach -> phone screen scheduled: within 48 hours of candidate reply.
- B: Phone screen -> first technical loop (on-site or virtual) scheduled: within 7 calendar days.
- C: Final interview -> hiring committee decision recorded in ATS: within 48 hours.
- D: Decision -> verbal offer extension: within 24 hours of decision (target).
- E: Written offer sent (ATS/Offer letter) -> candidate receives offer: within 48 hours of verbal.
- F: Offer acceptance target window: 7 calendar days (standardized unless counter-offer negotiation).

Why these numbers?
- Benchmarked against PLG SaaS peers and internal cycle times; goal is 30% faster time-to-offer vs historical while keeping interview quality.

Candidate touchpoint timeline (typical technical hire):
1) Application/Referral -> Recruiter outreach (Day 0-2):
   - Recruiter sends tailored intro message (template below).
   - If candidate replies, coordinator triggers scheduling link within 24 hrs.
2) Phone screen (Day 2-9):
   - 30-min recruiter screen or hiring manager screen to align expectations and compensation band.
   - Recruiter logs notes in ATS and adds three highlight bullets for hiring manager.
3) Technical loop (Day 5-14):
   - Ideally consolidated to 1–2 days (virtual) to reduce cognitive load.
   - Interviewers must submit feedback within 24 hours of slot. System sends automated reminder after 12 hours.
4) Hiring committee (Day 6-16):
   - Committee completes rubric scoring and records decision in ATS.
5) Offer phase (Day 6-18):
   - Recruiter coordinates with hiring manager and compensation to produce offer.
   - Recruiter delivers verbal offer + value props, then follows up with written offer within SLA above.

Owner map (who does what):
- Recruiter: owns candidate communication, scheduling, offer packaging coordination, and offer follow-ups.
- Recruiting Coordinator: scheduling, calendar wrangling, travel logistics (if onsite), document prep.
- Hiring Manager: interview scheduling availability, feedback submission, signoff on compensation within 24 hrs of request.
- Interviewers: focused, behaviorally-anchored feedback; submit within 24 hrs.
- People Ops Partner: escalations, compensation exceptions, equity/pricing signoff.

Templates (short):
- Initial outreach (recruiter): "Hi <name> — I'm Priya from Redwood Inference. We reviewed your work on <repo/paper>. We're hiring an SDE focused on inference systems; quick 20–30 min chat? Here's my calendar: <link>."
- Verbal offer script (bullet points recruit uses): role, comp band, equity overview, expected start window, relocation/remote note, next steps for written offer.

Interview feedback & scoring (lightweight rubric):
- Weighting: Technical competency 50% (problem solving, systems knowledge), Role fit 30% (domain experience, impact orientation), Culture/Leadership 20% (collaboration, ownership).
- Score range per interviewer: 1–5; must include at least 3 supporting bullets (strengths, areas to probe, risk).
- Hiring manager aggregates normalized score -> decision.

Offer packaging principles:
- Follow the published comp bands. If manager requests > band, they must: document business justification + get People Ops signoff.
- Equity offers standardized by level and tenure band. Keep transparency for internal candidates.
- Include clear start-date guidance and onboarding cohort notes where applicable.

Candidate experience checklist (pre-offer):
- All interviewers receive candidate resume + 3-line summary before interview.
- Recruiter sends thank-you note within 24 hrs of final interview summarizing timeline and next steps.
- Candidate receives ownership doc (one-pager) describing first 90 days for the role with the verbal offer.

Pre-hire operational checklist (items to complete before written offer):
- Comp signoff documented in ATS.
- Background check vendor form populated.
- Hiring manager confirms start window and relocation needs.
- Onboarding buddy assigned (if IC) or mentor (if manager).
- Equipment plan initiated with IT (list of required GPUs/VMs for infra hires).

Exceptions & escalations:
- If decision > 48 hrs after final interview: recruiter proactively notifies candidate with update and new ETA.
- For hard-to-fill roles (senior infra/applied-ML), offer velocity target extended to 10 business days but must have a documented cadence (weekly check-ins).
- If candidate requests >7 days to decide (e.g., counter offers), recruiter negotiates timeline and logs outcome in ATS.

Metrics to track (weekly) — minimal telemetry set we will report to People Ops and Hiring Managers:
- Time-to-offer median (application -> written offer).
- Interview-to-decision SLA compliance (% within 48 hrs).
- Offer acceptance rate by team/role.
- Candidate NPS (post-process survey).

Tooling notes (current integrations):
- ATS: Greenhouse (primary) — use "Offer Velocity" dashboard. Create automated reminders for feedback after 12 hrs.
- Calendar: Google Calendar + coordination via scheduling links (Calendly internal).
- Communication: Slack template channel #hiring-ops for escalations; use @people-ops for urgent signoffs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we centralize verbal-offer-approved checklists in Confluence vs keep in Greenhouse? (Priya to decide by 2026-03-15).
- Draft standard one-pager: 90-day role expectations (owner: Ethan).
- Create standardized offer-acceptance email template for international hires (Maria to draft).

Notes to self / heuristics (informal):
- Consolidate technical interviews into a single day when feasible — keeps momentum and improves acceptance.
- Always surface total comp (cash + equity) early in phone screen for senior roles.
- If a candidate is in multiple internal loops, prefer to sequence interviews and have shared interviewer notes to avoid redundancy.

Appendix: quick escalation matrix (names are placeholders):
- People Ops: Priya Nair (primary), Anika Singh (backup).
- Recruiting Leads: Ethan Caldwell (eng hires), María Gómez (product/design).

Change log (edits):
- 2025-11-12: initial draft created (Priya).
- 2025-12-05: added SLA targets and interview weighting (Ethan).
- 2026-01-20: included tooling notes and exceptions (María).
- 2026-03-01: updated targets and open-questions (Priya).

End of playbook — feedback welcome in doc comments.
